$comment: Machine-readable, bounded allow-list for Cratis/Components#176. Every entry names exact installed upstream package versions, diagnostic codes, resolution modes, source prefixes, and an objective removal condition. Components-owned diagnostics are covered only as explicitly paired cascades when the same compiler run contains the matching TS2834/TS2835 root cause in that exact upstream package; message similarity alone is insufficient. The verifier fails on unlisted diagnostics, metadata/version drift, unpaired owned diagnostics, and exceptions that stop reproducing.

upstreamIssues.summary: pixi.js bundles @webgpu/types, whose WebGPU ambient declarations duplicate identifiers TypeScript 6 and 7 ship in lib.dom.d.ts (GPUTextureFormat, GPUDevice, GPUBindGroupDescriptor.entries, ...) with incompatible shapes. TS7 reports individual TS2300 duplicates instead of TS6's grouped TS6200; its active platform library path is normalized to typescript/lib while the original path remains in the report.
upstreamIssues.reason: external - upstream declaration collision between @webgpu/types (a pixi.js dependency) and TypeScript's own built-in DOM lib; not a Components authoring defect.
upstreamIssues.removalCondition: pixi.js ships a @webgpu/types release whose WebGPU surface no longer duplicates conflicting global identifiers against the target TypeScript version's lib.dom.d.ts (tracked upstream at https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs and https://github.com/gpuweb/types), OR Components narrows Canvas's public renderItem/CanvasContext contract off raw PIXI.* types without losing the ability to render arbitrary Pixi content (rejected for now - see docs/ui-foundation.md, 'Why the Canvas Pixi surface is not narrowed').

upstreamIssues.summary: @cratis/arc.react ships a global.d.ts that declares `namespace JSX` referencing test-only ambient types (vitest/globals, chai, sinon-chai) as part of its published package instead of scoping that augmentation to its own test build. A strict external consumer that does not also install those test packages cannot resolve the bare `JSX` identifiers arc.react's dialog/command declaration files reference. This defect also surfaces under NodeNext since the extensionless specifiers were fixed.
upstreamIssues.reason: external - @cratis/arc.react's own shipped .d.ts, not a Components declaration; Components has no `namespace JSX` augmentation of its own.
upstreamIssues.removalCondition: A published @cratis/arc.react release removes (or properly scopes to its own test build) the global `namespace JSX` augmentation in global.d.ts, so `JSX.Element` in its public dialog/command declaration files resolves through @types/react's module-scoped JSX types instead.
